text_blocks.snippet: While there is no complete cure for Peyronie's disease, it can be treated to reduce symptoms and improve quality of life. Treatment options include medications, injections, traction therapy, and surgery, depending on the severity and progression of the condition. In some cases, mild cases may resolve on their own.
snippet_highlighted_words: there is no complete cure for Peyronie's disease

text_blocks.snippet: Peyronie's disease is characterized by the buildup of scar tissue (plaque) on the penis, causing curvature and potentially painful erections. While the disease can be painful and impact sexual function, it is treatable.

list.title: Medications:
list.snippet: Oral medications may help with pain, but they are not effective for correcting the curvature.

list.title: Injections:
list.snippet: Injecting medications like collagenase directly into the plaque can help to break down scar tissue and improve curvature.

list.title: Traction Therapy:
list.snippet: Using devices like penile traction devices can help to stretch the penis and improve curvature over time.

list.title: Surgery:
list.snippet: Surgery is typically considered for severe cases or when other treatments are not effective. Surgical options include plication, plaque incision, or penile implants.

list.title: Early treatment is important:
list.snippet: Early intervention can help prevent the disease from worsening and potentially lead to better outcomes.

list.title: Individualized treatment:
list.snippet: Treatment options are tailored to the individual patient's needs and the severity of their condition.

list.title: Consult with a specialist:
list.snippet: It's crucial to consult with a urologist or a specialist in male sexual health to discuss the best treatment options for Peyronie's disease.

text_blocks.snippet: Peyronie's disease is a condition where scar tissue (plaque) develops within the penis, causing it to curve or bend, especially during erections. This can lead to pain, erectile dysfunction, and difficulty with sexual intercourse. It's an acquired condition, meaning it develops over time, and is not present at birth.
snippet_highlighted_words: a condition where scar tissue (plaque) develops within the penis, causing it to curve or bend, especially during erections

list.snippet: Penile curvature: The most noticeable symptom, where the penis bends or curves during an erection.
Pain: Pain during erection or even at rest can occur.
Plaque formation: A palpable lump or area of scar tissue felt along the penis.
Erectile dysfunction: Difficulty achieving or maintaining an erection.
The exact cause is unknown, but it's believed to involve injury to the penis, possibly during intercourse or other activities.
There is also a possible link to connective tissue disorders.
A physical examination by a doctor is usually sufficient.
Ultrasound imaging may be used to assess the extent and location of the plaque.
Medical management: Injections of collagenase, a medication that breaks down scar tissue, are a common treatment.
Surgical options: Surgery may be necessary in severe cases to correct the curvature.
Penile traction therapy: Devices that gently stretch the penis can help improve curvature.

list.title: Prevalence:
list.snippet: It's estimated to affect up to 10% of men.

list.title: Impact:
list.snippet: Peyronie's disease can significantly impact a man's sexual health, self-esteem, and relationships.

list.title: Natural history:
list.snippet: While some cases may resolve on their own, many men will experience a worsening of symptoms without treatment.
